title: Normality or weak normality of cubic bent functions
summary: Determine whether every cubic bent function in every even dimension at least ten is normal or weakly normal.

formal_statement.body: For a Boolean function $f:\mathbb F_2^m\to\mathbb F_2$, define its relative degree on affine $r$-flats by $\deg_r(f)=\min_{a,V:\,\dim V=r}\deg(f|_{a+V})$. For every even $m\ge 10$ and every bent $f$ of algebraic degree exactly $3$, is $\deg_{m/2}(f)\le 1$? Equivalently, prove that every such $f$ is normal or weakly normal, or construct one with $\deg_{m/2}(f)\ge 2$.

scope.domain: Boolean bent functions and affine-flat normality
assumptions: Normality and weak normality use the source's affine-flat definitions
scope.unresolved_remainder: The full range of even dimensions m >= 10 remains open. In particular, the source-emphasized m = 10 case is not settled by the few known normal examples.

citations.label: Gillot--Langevin--Polujan, normality of 8-bit bent functions
citations.locator: Eq. (III.1) and Section VI, items 1-2, pp. 4363-4364

progress.summary: The source identifies dimension ten as the next open case and asks the same normal-or-weak-normal question for every even dimension at least ten.
